cancellationToken.param: Cancels the enumeration, which then throws .

state.para: Every enumeration is a subscription of its own: it subscribes when it starts and unsubscribes when it ends, by , an exception or cancellation. Errors of the SDK while subscribing are thrown when the enumeration starts. The loop body runs on the context of the enumerating code, not on a thread of the SDK.
Only the latest value the consumer didn't read yet is kept, older ones are skipped. The SDK can end the subscription on its own, the enumeration ends then.

stream.para: Every enumeration is a subscription of its own: it subscribes when it starts and unsubscribes when it ends, by , an exception or cancellation. Errors of the SDK while subscribing are thrown when the enumeration starts. The loop body runs on the context of the enumerating code, not on a thread of the SDK.
Every value is kept until the consumer reads it, the buffer grows while the consumer is slower than the SDK. The SDK can end the subscription on its own, the enumeration ends then.

loop.para: Every enumeration runs a loop of its own: it starts when the enumeration starts and stops when it ends, by , an exception or cancellation. The loop body runs on the context of the enumerating code, not on a thread of the SDK.
Every value is kept until the consumer reads it, the buffer grows while the consumer is slower than the SDK.

disposable.para: The values hold native objects and belong to the consumer: dispose them, or the native objects they contain, once they aren't needed anymore. Values that weren't yielded are disposed for you, values skipped by LINQ operators like Where or FirstAsync aren't.
